prompt:
I need the front end for Ondita. An audio-story maker for secondary-school language classes, where students record, cut and arrange clips into short radio-style pieces in the language they are learning.

Who's using it: Sofía Ramírez-Clark, a 10th grader in third-year Spanish who is comfortable on her phone but has never edited audio. Her teacher, Sr. Delgado, gives feedback through the same tool.

What they're doing right now: Her 3–4 minute 'Crónica de mi barrio' piece is due Friday. She has recorded an intro, two interviews with a neighbor and her abuela, and some street sounds. The draft runs 5:52, and Sr. Delgado's comment says the abuela interview runs long and the ending needs a closing line in her own voice. She's trimming the interviews down to the best answers, moving the market sounds under the intro, re-recording one line where she said 'el problema' wrong, and putting the segments in an order that tells a story, while watching that the total stays under 4:00.

What's in the system at this point: 14 clips in her project: intro narration (0:38), 3 narration takes for the middle section (0:22–0:31), interview with neighbor Don Arturo (1:47), interview with abuela Rosa (2:41), market street ambience (1:10), bus stop ambience (0:45), a 0:12 music sting from the class library, and 5 short pickup lines. Each clip has an automatic Spanish transcript with word timings, e.g. 'y cuando llegamos en el setenta y dos, todo era campo'. The current arrangement totals 5:52. Rubric: 4 criteria (content, pronunciation, use of past tenses, structure), 25 points each. Teacher comments are pinned to 3 moments in the draft. Due Friday, Nov 20, 11:59 p.m.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
